newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia says Belarus vote "normal", crisis averted.
newsitem.headline: Russia says Belarus vote "normal", crisis averted.

text.p: Russia greeted Belarus's controversial referendum on increasing President Alexander Lukashenko's powers as a "normal result" on Monday and concluded Moscow's bid to defuse the political crisis in Minsk had worked.

Asked for his assessment of Sunday's vote, which gave the president massive backing, Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said: "The main thing is that Belarus has given its assessment. I think it's a normal result. It's a matter for Belarus."
Earlier, he discussed the referendum results with President Boris Yeltsin.
The Kremlin press service said the two men stressed that Russia's "timely" efforts to mediate last week between Lukashenko and his parliamentary opponents had "prevented a social explosion".
Chernomyrdin brokered the compromise after all-night talks on Friday. But it fell apart within a day.

Chernomyrdin said on Sunday that a group of Belarus legislators were responsible for wrecking the accord, but also expressed irritation with Lukashenko for failing to do enough to make the accord work.

Moscow favors Lukashenko's quest for closer ties with Russia but fears his autocratic style and lack of free-market economic reforms could prove a burden in the two-state union agreed by Yeltsin and the Belarus president last April.

The Kremlin said Chernomyrdin met Yeltsin for an hour and a half at the Barvikha sanatorium near Moscow, where the president is convalescing. It is the longest reported working meeting Yeltsin has had since his heart bypass operation on November 5.
